identification.summary: Cisco Talos tracks UAT-9686 as a China-nexus advanced persistent threat cluster that exploited the AsyncOS zero-day CVE-2025-20393 (CVSS 10.0) in Cisco Secure Email Gateway (SEG) and Secure Email and Web Manager (SEWM) appliances where the Spam Quarantine feature was enabled and reachable from the internet [S1][S3][S8]. Cisco became aware of the activity on 2025-12-10; reporting says it had been active since at least late November 2025 (BankInfoSecurity says mid-November) [S8][S4].
identification.firstObserved: Active since at least late November 2025 (S4 says mid-November); Cisco became aware on 2025-12-10 [S4][S8].
identification.notes: UAT-9686 is a Talos-assigned uncategorized-threat designation; no Microsoft name or MITRE group id exists in this record. Talos reports tooling overlap with other Chinese-nexus activity (APT41, UNC5174) but does not merge the clusters [S8][S4]. Treat those overlaps as tooling similarities, not identity.

attribution.sponsor: China-nexus (state sponsorship not stated by a cited source) [S4][S8].
attribution.confidence: Talos assesses with moderate confidence that UAT-9686 is a Chinese-nexus APT; BankInfoSecurity words this as medium confidence [S4]. This is a vendor assessment only; no government attribution is cited here.
attribution.basis: Talos cites tooling and infrastructure overlaps with other Chinese-nexus groups; AquaTunnel (ReverseSSH-like reverse tunnel) has been linked to APT41 and UNC5174 [S8][S4].

targeting.notes: Cisco described the campaign as affecting a limited subset of appliances that run vulnerable AsyncOS with Spam Quarantine enabled and internet-exposed; that feature is not enabled by default [S2][S10][S3]. The cited sources gathered do not identify victim sectors, countries or numbers.

capabilities.summary: Zero-day exploitation of improper input validation in the AsyncOS Spam Quarantine feature, giving command execution with root privileges [S1][S3][S8]. Post-exploitation tooling reported by Talos: AquaShell (lightweight Python backdoor embedded in an existing file of a Python-based web server, executing encoded commands in the system shell), AquaTunnel (ELF reverse-SSH tunnel), Chisel (tunneling tool) and AquaPurge (log-clearing tool) [S8][S4]. Cisco's January 2026 fixes also remove persistence mechanisms installed in this campaign [S5][S9].

campaigns.summary: Cisco released fixes (for example SEG 15.0.5-016, 15.5.4-012, 16.0.4-016) that also remove persistence mechanisms installed in the campaign; reported by The Register and Security Affairs [S5][S9].

diamond.adversary: UAT-9686, China-nexus cluster assessed with moderate confidence by Talos [S4][S8].
diamond.capability: CVE-2025-20393 root-level exploitation; AquaShell, AquaTunnel, Chisel, AquaPurge [S8][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Reverse SSH and Chisel tunnels from compromised appliances; C2 details not captured in sources gathered [S8].
diamond.victim: Internet-exposed Cisco SEG/SEWM appliances with Spam Quarantine enabled, a limited subset [S2][S10].
diamond.technology: Email security appliances at the network edge running AsyncOS, with a non-default, internet-exposed Spam Quarantine feature [S2][S10][S3].

Victim sectors, countries, count and any data stolen are not public in the sources gathered; operator objective is not stated.

Relationship to APT41 and UNC5174 is tooling overlap only; cluster boundaries not resolved.
Exact CISA KEV date is from secondary sources (CISA site not opened).
Some sources disagree on the patch date (15 vs 16 January 2026).

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Email security gateways and quarantine managers sit at the network edge and see all mail flow, so they are key cyber terrain; the exposed non-default Spam Quarantine interface is the exposure [S2][S10]. STEP 2: The actor exploited a zero-day, then deployed persistent backdoor, tunnels and log purging, so defenders had no patch for about a month [S8][S5]. STEP 3: Likely sequence from the sources: exploit quarantine interface, root access, AquaShell, AquaTunnel/Chisel reverse tunnel, AquaPurge log clearing [S8][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA: continued targeting of exposed edge appliances for persistent access. MDCOA: use of compromised mail gateways to read or manipulate mail of high-value organizations. Candidate indicators: Spam Quarantine reachable from the internet, unexpected modification of the Python web server files, outbound reverse SSH or Chisel sessions from the appliance, gaps in appliance logs [S8][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: inventory Cisco SEG/SEWM and check Spam Quarantine exposure; Cisco's guidance was to open a TAC case to check for compromise [S10]. (2) Authorities: KEV-driven directives set deadlines for federal civilian agencies; confirm DoD equivalents [S3]. (3) Mission assurance: fixed builds also remove persistence, but compromised appliances may need rebuild decisions with the vendor [S5][S9]. (4) Coordination: share indicators through DC3 and the DIB program; note that attribution is a vendor assessment of moderate confidence [S4].

provenance.importedSummary: UAT-9686 is a Chinese state-sponsored APT known for targeting networking infrastructure and edge appliances through a sophisticated espionage campaign. They exploit a critical flaw in the Cisco AsyncOS Spam Quarantine interface to gain root access and deploy custom malware, including AquaShell, along with Python scripts that execute natively. Their operations involve reverse tunneling and log purging, demonstrating a methodical approach to compromising communication infrastructure. Talos has observed overlaps in TTPs and tooling with other Chinese-nexus threat actors, indicating a consistent operational pattern.
